title: 2020 AMC 12A Problem 22
statement: Let \((a_n)\) and \((b_n)\) be the sequences of real numbers such that \[(2 + i)^n = a_n + b_n i\] for all integers \(n \ge 0,\) where \(i = \sqrt{-1}.\) What is \[\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{a_n b_n}{7^n}?\]

solutions.text:
Since \((a_n + b_n i)^2 = a_n^2 - b_n^2 + 2 a_n b_n i,\) we have \(a_n b_n\) \(= \tfrac12 \operatorname{Im}\big((2 + i)^{2n}\big)\) \(= \tfrac12 \operatorname{Im}\big((3 + 4i)^n\big).\)

Therefore the sum is \(\tfrac12 \operatorname{Im} \displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \left(\frac{3 + 4i}{7}\right)^n\) \(= \tfrac12 \operatorname{Im}\!\left(\frac{1}{1 - \frac{3 + 4i}{7}}\right).\)

This equals \(\tfrac12 \operatorname{Im}\!\left(\dfrac{7}{4 - 4i}\right)\) \(= \tfrac12 \operatorname{Im}\!\left(\dfrac{7(4 + 4i)}{32}\right)\) \(= \tfrac12 \cdot \dfrac{28}{32}\) \(= \dfrac{7}{16}.\)

Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: Since \((2 + i)^2 = 3 + 4i,\) the sum becomes a geometric series with ratio \(\dfrac{3 + 4i}{7}\)
